posts.title: Walking in covenant: God keeps His promises
posts.excerpt: A covenant is more than a contract — it is a relationship sealed by love. Here is what that means for you this week.
posts.body:
Throughout Scripture, God reveals Himself as a covenant-keeping God. When He made a promise to Abraham, He bound Himself by His own name, because there was no one greater to swear by (Hebrews 6:13).

Covenant is relationship

A contract says, “I will do my part if you do yours.” A covenant says, “I am yours, and you are mine.” That is the heart of the Gospel: in Christ, God has drawn us into His family.

“Know therefore that the Lord your God, He is God, the faithful God who keeps covenant and mercy for a thousand generations with those who love Him.” — Deuteronomy 7:9

Living it out

This week, take a moment each morning to thank God for one promise He has kept in your life. Share it with someone in your family or small group. Faith grows when testimonies are spoken.
posts.author: Bishop Henry Muzhari

posts.title: Five ways to pray for your family this week
posts.excerpt: Simple, Scripture-based prayers you can pray over your home, your marriage and your children.
posts.body:
Prayer is the foundation of a strong home. Here are five simple ways to pray for your family this week:

  1. For peace — “Let the peace of God rule in your hearts” (Colossians 3:15).
  2. For protection — pray Psalm 91 over every member of your household.
  3. For unity — ask God to knit your hearts together in love.
  4. For provision — thank God in advance for meeting every need.
  5. For purpose — pray that each child discovers the calling God has placed on their life.

Join us this Sunday as we stand together in prayer for our families.
posts.author: Reverend Eunice Muzhari
